EXPLANATION: The dominant Raman line at 2220 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a C≡N stretch; candidate 2 contains a nitrile group (N#C) while several higher-ranked candidates do not. The weak but clear band at 3376 cm⁻¹ fits the N–H stretching region of a primary aromatic amine (NH₂) present only in candidate 2; it would not be produced by candidates lacking N–H or terminal ≡C–H. The 1605 cm⁻¹ peak matches the NH₂ scissoring / aromatic C=C stretch typical of anilines, and the 1319 cm⁻¹ and 1180 cm⁻¹ bands coincide with C–N stretches and ring modes found in para-substituted anilines. Bands near 847 cm⁻¹ and 657–700 cm⁻¹ correspond to NH₂ wagging/twisting and substituted-ring out-of-plane motions, again expected for an aromatic amine. Overall the peak pattern (nitrile stretch + primary amine stretches/bends + aromatic modes) is most consistent with N#Cc1ccc(N)cc1.
